STK38L.functional_summary: Phosphorylates Rabin8 which is crucial role in ciliogenesis. Regulates the process of vesicular trafficking and tethering to the pericentrosome, promoting local activation of Rab8 and ciliary membrane formation. Defects in NDR2-mediated Rabin8 phosphorylation impair preciliary membrane assembly and ciliogenesis, leading to accumulation of Rabin8-/Rab11-containing vesicles at the pericentrosome. Knockdown in RPE1 cells suporesses ciliogenesis (23435566, 28122914). Mutated in canine early reti l degeneration, suggesting a role in photoreceptor cell function (20887780).; A serine/threonine kinase (NDR2) crucial for early ciliogenesis. Promotes cilia formation by phosphorylating Rab-binding protein Rabin8, thereby activating the small GTPase Rab8 at the centrosome(28122914).

TLCD3B.functional_summary: Mutations in the TLCD3B gene cause Cone-Rod Dystrophy (PMID: 33077892).

TMEM107.functional_summary: Critical regulator of cilia formation and morphology (26518474). Controls ciliary proteincomposition. Functions redundantly with NPHP4 to regulate cilium integrity, transition zone docking and assembly of membrane to microtubule Y- link connectors. Recruits ciliopathy proteins MKS1, TMEM231 and TMEM237. Mutated in OFD and JBTS patients (26595381). In mice, mutations decrease cilia number and disrupt Hh sig ling. Essential for craniofacial development (28954202). Acts synergistically with Gli2 as a positive mediator of Shh and ciliogenesis (22698544). Loss of Tmem107 results in disruption in early L- R patterning events at the node (31887266).
TMEM107.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Meckel syndrome; leukoencephalopathy with calcifications and cysts; Meckel syndrome 13

TMEM138.functional_summary: Mutations cause JBTS. Required for ciliogenesis. Mutations lead to shorter cilia, and knockdown cells show defects of ciliogenesis. It might mark vesicles en route to the base of cilium, which is known to be crucial for ciliary assembly (22282472).

TMEM17.functional_summary: CEP-290-dependent transition zone protein that facilitates cilium formation, being necessary for ciliogenesis, mutated in OFD6 (26982032). Specifically, PC from OFD6 patient cells are longer with altered protein composition and impaired ability to transduce the Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) pathway. We further modeled the Arg94Trp variant in a C. elegans model system, as well as the two previously reported variants (Gly101Val and Asn102Lys) with unknown pathological mechanisms [39, 41], and found that all three disrupt TMEM-17 function. Together, our findings establish TMEM17 as a bona fide ciliopathy gene with a broad phenotypic spectrum and provide evidence that deleterious missense variants in TMEM17 involve amino acids that reside within a transmembrane “mutational hotspot” crucial for its biological function. (40841990)

TMEM216.functional_summary: Required for ciliogenesis. It might mark vesicles en route to the base of cilium, which is known to be crucial for ciliary assembly. Mutations cause JBTS (22282472). Mutated in OFD6 (26982032) and in Meckel syndrome MKS (21493627). Mutations or knockdown result in impaired ciliogenesis and centrosome docking. Modulates hyper- responsiveness of sig ling pathways mediated by Dvl and RhoA, suggesting they might be part of a complex to mediate cellular polarization and centrosomal apical docking (20512146).
TMEM216.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Joubert syndrome; Joubert syndrome 2; Meckel syndrome, type 2; Meckel syndrome; Joubert syndrome with oculorenal defect

TMEM218.functional_summary: MKS module component, TMEM-218 (Tmem218), that requires CEP-290 and other MKS module components for TZ localisation and functions together with the NPHP module to facilitate ciliogenesis(26982032).

TMEM231.functional_summary: Interacts with several JBTS proteins as part of the B9 complex, involved in the formation of the diffusion barrier between the cilia and plasma membrane, maintaining the integrity of the cilia. Knockdown results in a reduction of cilia formation, and perturbs localisation of components of the B9 complex at the transition zone and ciliary localisation of sig lling receptors. Mutations have been associated with JBTS (23012439). Mutated in MKS (23349226). Critical for organizing the MKS complex and controlling ciliary composition. Mutated in OFD3. In mice, mutations disrupt the localisation of proteins Arl13b and Inpp5e to cilia (25869670).
TMEM231.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Joubert syndrome with ocular defect; Meckel syndrome; Joubert syndrome 20; Joubert syndrome with oculorenal defect; Meckel syndrome, type 11; ciliopathy; Joubert syndrome and related disorders

TMEM237.functional_summary: Also known as JBTS-14 . Interacts functio lly with NPHP4, MKS2, MKSR1, MKSR2, and MKS5 at the transition zone. Its interaction with NPHP4 promotes basal body-TZ attachment to the membrane and cilium formation. Loss of TMEM237 results in defective ciliogenesis and deregulation of Wnt sig ling. Mutated in Joubert syndrome related disorders (22152675).
TMEM237.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Joubert syndrome; Joubert syndrome 14; Joubert syndrome with oculorenal defect
TMEM237.mouse_ciliopathy_phenotype: abnormal reti morphology, abnormal testis morphology, abnormal heart morphology, enlarged heart, abnormal adrel gland morphology, small adrel glands, abnormal brain morphology, small testis, increased circulating aspartate transamise level

TMEM240.functional_summary: Mutations in the TMEM240 gene cause Spinocerebellar Ataxia (PMID: 25070513).
TMEM240.mouse_ciliopathy_phenotype: abnormal testis morphology, small testis, abnormal liver morphology

TMEM67.functional_summary: Also known as Meckelin or MKS3. Component of the MKS-JBTS module at the transition zone. Essential for phosphorylation of the non- canonical Wnt receptor ROR2. Negative regulator of Shh sig lling. Required for centriolar migration to the apical membrane during cell polarisation, regulation of actin cytoskeleton remodelling and RhoA activity (26035863). Required for the elongation and mainte nce of the outer segments in reti . It may play a role in photoreceptor intraciliary transport (22247471). Mutations are a major cause of MKS, JBTS and NPHP (23393159). MKS function is required for ciliary structure and function, plays a role in regulating cilia length and number through modulating centrosome duplication (19515853). In complex with other TZ proteins, it contributes to an early ciliogenic event and establish basal body/TZ membrane attachments (21422230).
TMEM67.protein_complex: MKS1-TMEM67 complex; SYNE2-TMEM67 complex; DNAJB9-DNAJC10-TMEM67 complex
TMEM67.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Joubert syndrome with hepatic defect; nephronophthisis 11; Meckel syndrome, type 3; Joubert syndrome 6; Meckel syndrome; Joubert syndrome; Bardet-Biedl syndrome 14; Nephronophthisis; nephronophthisis; Joubert syndrome and related disorders
curation_notes: Assigned to 'Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease' per user CSV granularity (v12)

TMEM72.functional_summary: Immunohistochemistry staining of kidney biopsies revealed altered localization and expression of TMEM72 in cases compared to controls. In human-derived tubuloids, we showed that TMEM72 localizes to the cilium. Furthermore, using an affinity proteomics approach, we found an association of TMEM72 and ciliary function, more specifically in selective ciliary cholesterol transport(41308066).

TNP1.functional_summary: Although nuclear thiol status appears to be unchanged in Tnp mutants, tail structure abnormalities observed in mutant sperm samples indicate an altered thiol status in the flagella. In TPl knockout mutant epididymal sperm, bent midpieces and midpieces with gaps between mitochondria are observed when examined using light microscopy. In TP2 knockout mutant sperm many tails are observed to be unraveled. The same abnormalities are identified at higher magnification using electron microscopy. Observations made during this study also provide evidence that thiol status is altered at some point during cell maturation since structural integrity of mutant sperm midpieces are disrupted following treatment with DTT. After reduction of thiols, mitochondria are noticeably absent from midpieces of TPl knockout mutant sperm. A similar but lesser effect is observed in sperm from the TP2 knockout mutant().

TNP2.functional_summary: Although nuclear thiol status appears to be unchanged in Tnp mutants, tail structure abnormalities observed in mutant sperm samples indicate an altered thiol status in the flagella. In TPl knockout mutant epididymal sperm, bent midpieces and midpieces with gaps between mitochondria are observed when examined using light microscopy. In TP2 knockout mutant sperm many tails are observed to be unraveled. The same abnormalities are identified at higher magnification using electron microscopy. Observations made during this study also provide evidence that thiol status is altered at some point during cell maturation since structural integrity of mutant sperm midpieces are disrupted following treatment with DTT. After reduction of thiols, mitochondria are noticeably absent from midpieces of TPl knockout mutant sperm. A similar but lesser effect is observed in sperm from the TP2 knockout mutant().

TOGARAM1.description: TOG array regulator of axonemal 1 [Source:HGNC Symbol,Acc:HGNC:19959]
ciliopathies: Neural tube defects with ciliary dysfunction
TOGARAM1.functional_summary: Mutated in JBTS37. TOGARAM1 localized along the ciliary axoneme in hTERT-RPE1 cells and was associated with longer cilia when knocked down. Binds directly to ARMC9, forming a protein module that localizes to microtubule-like structures at the centriole and proximal portion of the cilium. The interaction with ARMC9 mapped to the N-termi l protein of TOGARAM1 (32453716, 32747439).The length of cilia was normal in the FAP256-KO, reduced (by 16%) in CHE12-KO and increased (by 14%) in ARMC9-KO cells (PMID: 30217954).
curation_notes: Wang et al. 2025 (PMID 39385469): TOGARAM1 expressed in neural tube; KO mice show neural tube closure defects, abnormal cilia, reduced SHH signaling. Patient with TOGARAM1 variant had spina bifida.

Disease label renamed: 'Spina Bifida / Neural Tube Defects' → 'Neural tube defects with ciliary dysfunction' to reflect candidate-level evidence (n=1 patient with TOGARAM1 variant) and mechanistic specificity

TOPORS.description: TOP1 binding arginine/serine rich protein, E3 ubiquitin ligase [Source:HGNC Symbol,Acc:HGNC:21653]
TOPORS.functional_summary: Component of the photoreceptor sensory cilium. Potential role in the regulation of primary cilia-dependent photoreceptor development and function. Knockdown leads to increased cell death in the reti of zebrafish (21159800). Mutations have been associated with autosomal domi nt retinitis pigmentosa (17924349, 18509552).
TOPORS.mouse_ciliopathy_phenotype: female infertility, abnormal auditory brainstem response, cataract

TP73.functional_summary: Also called P73. Might be critical for the initiation of cilia assembly by indirectly promoting the multiplication of centrosomes (25201258). Transcription factor critical to multiciliogenesis. Required for multiciliated cells differentiation, function and for the direct regulation of transcriptio l modulators of multiciliogenesis, including Foxj1, Rfx2 and Rfx3 (31028178, 27257214, 26947080). Required for basal body docking, axonemal extension and motility (27257214).

TRAF3IP1.functional_summary: Also known as IFT54. Evolucio irly conserved role in ciliogenesis, interacts with with tubulin and actin. Mutations lead to altered cilia mediated hedgehog sig ling (21945076). Plays a critical role in IFT, as well as building and maintaining functio l cilia (18369462). IFT-B subunit which regulates ciliary composition. I ctivation is embryonic lethal and causes characteristic ciliopathy phenotypes (26487268). Interacts with and stabilises IFT20 and Rabaptin5, which in turn interacts with Rab8, suggesting a potential role for IFT in regulating the assembly of ciliary membranes. It may also participate in tubulin transport for ciliogenesis. Loss of IFT54 impairs cilia assembly as well as cytoplasmic MT dy mics (28417161). Interacts with both kinesin鈥怚I and IFT dynein and regulates anterograde IFT (33368450).

TRIM32.functional_summary: I ctivating homozygous mutations cause ciliopathy BBS11 (16606853). Ubiquiti tes NPHP5 which triggers protein delocalization and loss of cilia. Loss of BBS11 causes an accumulation of NPHP5 at the centrosome (28498859).

TRPV4.description: transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily V member 4 [Source:HGNC Symbol,Acc:HGNC:18083]
TRPV4.functional_summary: Mediates Ca2+ influx in response to mechanical and osmotic stimuli in ciliated epithelia, which in turns regulates the ciliary beat frequency (18719094). Mediates oscillatory fluid shear mechanotransduction in various cells via the primary cilium (29491434).

TSC1.functional_summary: Regulates the length of cilia. Form a complex with TSC2 that negatively regulates the nTOR pathway and, in turn, cell growth, proliferation and survival (19008302). Mutations have been associated with Tuberous sclerosis complex and polycystic kidney disease. Loss of Tsc1 or Tsc2 enhances ciliary formation and elongation (18845692). Required for activation of canonical TGF-尾 sig ling. Regulates Smoothened (SMO)- dependent HH sig ling in cilia (29396625). Role in maintaining cell polarity (19321600).
functional_category: Trafficking (BBSome, small GTPases, vesicular transport, ATPases)

Loss of Tsc1 or Tsc2 enhances ciliary formation and elongation (18845692). Regulates Smoothened (SMO)- dependent HH sig ling in cilia (29396625). Role in maintaining cell polarity. Associates with the GSK3/axin complex to inhibit canonical Wnt-sig lling (19321600). Required for the normal trafficking of PC-1 from the Golgi to the membrane (20169078).

TSGA10.functional_summary: Role in spermatogenesis. Possible role in the structure of primary cilium, as it was found to colocalise with gamma- tubulin in COS-1 cells (16643851).

TSSK1B.functional_summary: TSSK1B has localized in basal body, transition zone.

TTBK2.functional_summary: Regulator of the initiation of ciliogenesis in vivo. Ttbk2 mutants lack cilia. Promotes the removal of CP110 from the mother centriole, the recruitment and retention of IFT proteins at the distal end of basal body, to initiate the assembly of the ciliary axoneme (23141541). Mutations have been associated with domi nt human neurodegenerative disorder Spinocerebellar Ataxia type 11 (18037885). Interacts in a complex with CP164, which is required for its ciliary localisation. Promotes assembly of distal appendages at both centrioles and Cep83 localisation (24982133). Phosphorylates Cep164, Cep97 and inhibits the interaction between Cep164 and Dvl3 (25297623). Phosphorylated CEP83, which is required for ciliary vesicle docking and CP110 removal (31455668). To investigate if elevated TTBK2 expression promoted ciliogenesis or extended cilia length, cells were subjected to serum starvation to induce cilia formation, but neither cilia formation nor cilia length was affected by TTBK2 overexpression (Fig. 3E–G), indicating that the increased frequency of ciliation by TTBK2 overexpression was not attributable to a promotion of ciliogenesis or cilia elongation.ciliogenesis, to regulate cilium stability (30532139). To examine if TTBK2 kinase activity is required for its function in GNP proliferation, we mutated TTBK2 residue D163 from aspartic acid to alanine (TTBK2KD) [24, 26] and expressed TTBK2KD in GNPs. Surprisingly, a majority of TTBK2KD-expressing cells exited the cell cycle and migrated prematurely to the IGL, indicating that TTBK2-dependent GNP proliferation relies on TTBK2 activity (Fig. 2E, F). By performing Arl13b staining, TTBK2 overexpression in GNPs increased the percentage of ciliated GNPs, indicating that elevated TTBK2 levels in GNPs stabilize primary cilia (Figs. 2G and S2B). Furthermore, in developing cerebella electroporated with TTBK2KD, proportions of ciliated GNPs were greatly reduced (Figs. 2G and S2B), confirming that TTBK2 supports GNP proliferation through TTBK2’s activity-dependent stabilization of primary cilia. (38879724)

TTC12.functional_summary: Centrosome component (23300604). Involved in the assembly and/or transport of axonemal dynein arms. Loss of function affects both ODA and IDA. In paramecia, knockdown led to the absence of dynein arms (31978331).

TTC17.functional_summary: Interacts with C2orf62 and regulates ciliogenesis and actin polymerisation in ciliated cells. Depletion reduces the number of primary cilia but does not alter their length (24475127).

TTC21A.functional_summary: With ciliary axonemes and centrioles labeled with anti-Ac-α-tubulin and anti-γ-tubulin, respectively, we found that cilium length was reduced after Cep78, Ift20, or Ttc21a knockdown and could be rescued by exogenous expression of Cep78syn-HA, Ift20syn-Flag, and Ttc21asyn-Flag . Cep78, Ift20, and Ttc21a located in the base of the cilium (PMID: 36756949). The TTC21A-associated morphological abnormalities affect sperm flagella and head-tail conjunction. The detailed molecular contributions of TTC21A to sperm flagellar formation and intraflagellar transport need to be further investigated in future studies (PMID: 30929735).
functional_category: Motile cilium & axoneme; Non-motile cilium / primary cilium

TTC21B.functional_summary: Encodes a retrograde intraflagellar transport-A complex, associates with the motor protein dynein2 to regulate retrograde trafficking in the primary cilium. Knockdown induces microtubule anchoring defects (24876116). Mutated in nephronophthisis, syndromic Jeune Asphyxiating Thoracic Dystrophy (21258341), Focal Segmental glomerulosclerosis (24876116) and Joubert Syndrome (29615573).
functional_category: Trafficking (BBSome, small GTPases, vesicular transport, ATPases)

TTC29.functional_summary: Also known as NYD-SP14. Strongly expressed in tissues with motile cilia and flagella. Functions in cilia and flagella, most likely as an inner-arm dynein subunit. Chlamydomo s homologue encodes 44kDa subunit of axonemal dynein (17981992). Involved in functio l interaction with the IFT machinery, participating in anterograde IFT. Mutations have been associated with multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella (31735294).

TTC8.functional_summary: Also known as BBS8. Component of the BBSome complex, interacts with PCM1. Mutations leads to Bardet-Biedl syndrome with randomization of left-right body axis symmetry (14520415). Role in intraciliary/flagellar transport, coordi ting the velocity of the kinesin molecular motors during anterograde transport. Interacts with Vangl2 to establish and maintain of vertebrate left-right asymmetry. It may also be responsible for maintaining normal cilium length in the KV but not cilia number (20643117). Required for the development, mainte nce and survival of photoreceptors and outer segments in both rods and cones (29126234). Knockdown reduces ciliary length and increases levels of HDAC6 (30446775).
functional_category: Trafficking (BBSome, small GTPases, vesicular transport, ATPases)

TTC8.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Bardet-Biedl syndrome; retinitis pigmentosa; Bardet-Biedl syndrome 1

TTLL3.functional_summary: Functions in posttranslatio l glycylation of . Required for either elongation or stability of axonemes (19531357). Depletion leads to shortening and loss of axonemes (21262966). Required for primary cilia formation and control of cell proliferation. Only glycylase expressed in colon (25180231).
TTLL3.evidence_flag: TOF: burden analysis only (Zhou 2025); mouse model not yet performed

TTLL5.functional_summary: Recruited by ARL13B and FIP5 (30120249). Higher activity initiating glutamate chains than elongating them. Required for RPGRORF15 function as it seems to be highly selective (27162334). Essential for the correct function of sperm flagella. It might also be responsible for the tubulin polyglutami tion in the microtubule triplets of the centrioles, increasing the centriole stability. Mutations have been identified as cause of recessive reti l dystrophy (24791901), and reduced sperm motility and infertility in humans (28173158). TTLL5 localizes to photoreceptor connecting cilium; variants cause cone/cone-rod dystrophy. Glutamylase for tubulin in photoreceptor outer segment cilia. Macular sheen phenotype on SD-OCT characteristic.

TUB.functional_summary: Mutations have been associated with reti l and cochlear degeneration, as well as obesity (24375934). Function in ciliary GPCR trafficking in a similar way to TULP3 (28154160).
functional_category: Trafficking (BBSome, small GTPases, vesicular transport, ATPases)

TUBB.functional_summary: Forms β-tubulin of microtubules, essential cytoskeleton component. Pathogenic variants alter microtubule dynamics, impairing early ciliogenesis and leading to ciliopathy-like phenotypes (e.g., in kidney and cerebellum)(41309602). TULP4 has localized in flagella.; TUBB has localized in basal body.
functional_category: Ciliary assembly/disassembly; Cilia???cytoskeleton/adhesion links; Ciliary assembly/disassembly

TUBB3.functional_summary: Beta tubulin isoform. Component of the cytoskeleton, centrosomes and protofilaments, structures that associate laterally to form a microtubule.
functional_category: Trafficking (BBSome, small GTPases, vesicular transport, ATPases)

TUBB4B.functional_summary: Beta tubulin isoform. Component of the cytoskeleton, centrosomes and protofilaments, structures that associate laterally to form a microtubule. Mutations in TUBB4B Cause a Distinctive Sensorineural Disease of LCA with hearing loss TUBB4B variants cause PCD (12 patients) and LCA in dominant-negative manner. Distinct variants differentially affect microtubule dynamics and cilia formation, stratifying patients into 3 classes of ciliopathic disease. TUBB4B is a distinct tubulin isotype with organelle-specific function in axonemal microtubules (PMID:38662826).

TUBGCP4.functional_summary: Also known as GCP4. Required for the initial assembly of gamma-tubulin ring complexes and for their stabilization after assembly. These complexes are used as templates for the longitudi l association with 伪/尾-tubulin dimers during the nucleation process (29514869, 32317396). Associates with gamma-tubulin small complexes, GCP5 and GCP6 (21725292). Mutations have been identified in patients with autosomal- recessive microcephaly and chorioretinopathy. Role in mainte nce of reti l homeostasis, through participating in assembly of gamma- TuRC (31209365).

TUBGCP6.functional_summary: Also known as GCP6. Required for the initial assembly of gamma-tubulin ring complexes and for their stabilization after assembly. These complexes are used as templates for the longitudi l association with 伪/尾-tubulin dimers during the nucleation process (29514869, 32317396). Associates with gamma-tubulin small complexes, GCP4 and GCP5 (21725292).

TULP1.functional_summary: Role in intracellular transport, cell differentiation, sig ling, and motility. Mutations result in progressive photoreceptor degeneration in mice and retinitis pigmentosa in humans (33187986, 25074776, 9462750).

TULP3.functional_summary: Role in intracellular transport, cell differentiation, sig ling, and motility (33187986). Associates with IFT-A in a complex to regulate trafficking and localisation of G protein-coupled receptors into cilia. Negative regulator of Hedgehog sig ling (20889716). Adapter for ciliary trafficking of membrane cargo, regulates PC1/2 complex trafficking (28154160). Required for proper Shh-dependent limb patterning, as it inhibits Gli2 activity (19286674). Essential for trafficking of Arl13b and INPP5E into cilia. Loss of function causes ciliopathy-associated polycystic kidney disease, downregulates the formation of cilia and their length (30799240, 30583862).
functional_category: Trafficking (BBSome, small GTPases, vesicular transport, ATPases)

TULP3.mouse_ciliopathy_phenotype: increased circulating alanine transamise level, increased circulating bilirubin level, increased circulating aspartate transamise level

TULP4.functional_summary: WDR35 is homologous to TULP4 (from the Tubby superfamily) and has previously been characterized as an intraflagellar transport component, confirming that Sensenbrenner syndrome is a ciliary disorder (PMID: 20817137). Conserved domain in the amino terminus enables some members of the tubby family (TULP3, TULP2 and TUB but not TULP1 and TULP4) to bind to ciliary IFT-A(PMID: 20889716). TULP4 has localized in flagella.

TUSC3.functional_summary: Rare variants were present in multiple genes distinct from those with BA-associated common variants in most BA cases. AFAP1 and TUSC3 knockdown blocked ciliogenesis in mouse tracheal cells. Inhibition of ciliogenesis caused biliary dysgenesis in zebrafish. AFAP1 and TUSC3 were expressed in fetal liver organoids, as well as fetal and BA livers, but not in normal or disease-control livers. Integrative analysis of BA-associated variants and liver transcripts revealed abnormal vasculogenesis and epithelial tube formation, explaining portal vein anomalies that co-exist with BA(37572794).

TXNDC15.functional_summary: Mutated in patients with Meckel-Gruber syndrome (27894351, 30851085, 31411728). Loss of TXNDC15 prevented correct localization of the TMEM67 ciliary receptor to the transition zone (27894351).

UBAP1L.functional_summary: Mutations in the UBAP1L gene cause Cone-Rod Dystrophy (PMID: 38293907).

UMOD.functional_summary: Mutations are responsible for medullary cystic kidney disease type 2 (15029248), familial juvenile hyperuricemic nephropathy and glomerulocystic kidney disease. Expressed in re l primary cilia. UMOD mutations result in decreased ciliary uromodulin expression and delayed ER to Golgi trafficking (20172860 ).
functional_category: Trafficking (BBSome, small GTPases, vesicular transport, ATPases)
UMOD.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: kidney disease; autosomal dominant medullary cystic kidney disease with or without hyperuricemia; chronic kidney disease; kidney failure

USH1C.description: USH1 protein network component harmonin [Source:HGNC Symbol,Acc:HGNC:12597]
USH1C.functional_summary: Mutation are associated with Usher syndrome type 1c (16464467). Binds to myosin VIIa,cadherin 23 and F-actin (12588794).
USH1C.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 18A; hearing loss, autosomal recessive

USH1G.description: USH1 protein network component sans [Source:HGNC Symbol,Acc:HGNC:16356]
USH1G.functional_summary: Ciliopathy gene OMIM: 607696. Mutation are associated with Usher syndrome type 1g. Associates with harmonin and is involved in the functio l network formed through it (12588794). Required for outer segment differentiation, formation and mainte nce of reti and photoreceptor cell polarity. Scaffold protein in the USH network during ciliogenesis, as dysfunction leads to reti l degeneration (17923142). Form a complex with myomegalin, cooperating in the vesicle transport towards the ciliary base of photoreceptor cells (21767579). Interacts directly with IFT-B proteins, IFT20, IFT52, IFT57, and IFT74, ISHG1 may control the transport of these molecules to the ciliary base (31637240).

USH2A.functional_summary: MIM: 608400 (10738000) Required for the long-term mainte nce of reti l photoreceptors (17360538). Interacts and colocalises with Nlp and lebercilin at the centrosome (18826961). Interacts with SPAG5 and NINL to regulate microtubule-based cytoplasmic trafficking of proteins required for ciliogenesis, mainte nce and/or function, to the apical inner segment and basal body of photoreceptor. Mutations are associated withnon- syndromic retinitis pigmentosa and Usher syndrome (23351521).
functional_category: Trafficking (BBSome, small GTPases, vesicular transport, ATPases)

USP11.functional_summary: USP11 staining was observed in the cytoplasm and cilia(31835165).

USP45.functional_summary: Mutations in the USP45 gene cause Leber Congenital Amaurosis (PMID: 30573563).

VHL.functional_summary: MIM: 193300, MIM: 144700, MIM: 171300, MIM: 263400, Somatic i ctivation of VHL causes re l and pancreatic cysts associated with cilia loss. Stabilises microtubule dy mics in the axoneme (17450132). Interacts with KIF3A and kinesin.
VHL.protein_complex: ELOB-ELOC-USP33-VHL complex; VHL-TBP1-HIF1A complex; EGLN1-HIF1A-PLD1-VHL complex; AKAP9-EGLN1-HIF1A-VHL complex; ELOB-ELOC-HIF1A-VHL complex; HIF1A-VHL complex; ELOB-ELOC-VHL complex; EPAS1-VHL complex; EGLN1-LIMD1-VHL complex; Ubiquitin E3 ligase (VHL, TCEB1, TCEB2, CUL2); Ubiquitin E3 ligase (VHL, TCEB1, TCEB2, CUL2, RBX1); EGLN1-HIF1A-LIMD1-RHOBTB3 complex; CUL2-ELOB-EGLN1-LIMD1-VHL complex
VHL.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: clear cell renal carcinoma; adrenal gland pheochromocytoma; nonpapillary renal cell carcinoma; renal cell carcinoma

WDPCP.description: WD repeat containing planar cell polarity effector [Source:HGNC Symbol,Acc:HGNC:28027]
WDPCP.functional_summary: MIM: 613580. Also known as C2ORF86, BBS15 or FRITZ. Regulates pla r cell polarity through the modulation of the actin cytoskeleton. Required for recruitment of proteins essential for ciliogenesis to the transition zone, including Sept2, Nphp1, and Mks1, and facilitates the assembly of multiprotein complexes. Mutations have been associated with Bardet-Biedl and and Meckel-Gruber syndromes (24302887, 32055034). Knockdown leads to fewer and shorter cilia and decreses the expression of Septin7 in human sal epithelium, indication that Septin7 could be a target of WDPCP (28001338). Regulates cilia function and beating through activation of MAPK/ERK pathway in the mitochondria of sino sal epithelial cells (33598458).
WDPCP.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Bardet-Biedl syndrome 15; Bardet-Biedl syndrome; Meckel syndrome

WDR11.functional_summary: Modulates the Hedgehog (Hh) sig lling pathway and is essential for ciliogenesis. It may be required for cilia extension and growth. Interacts with ciliary components involved in human ciliopathies such as BBSomes and IFT proteins. Shuttles between cilium and nucleus in response to Shh sig lling. Implicated in congenital hypogo dotropic hypogo dism (CHH) and Kallmann syndrome (KS), characterised by delayed puberty and infertility (29263200).
functional_category: Trafficking (BBSome, small GTPases, vesicular transport, ATPases)
WDR11.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: isolated congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; hypogonadotropic hypogonadism 14 with or without anosmia
WDR11.mouse_ciliopathy_phenotype: enlarged kidney, abnormal heart morphology, abnormal liver morphology, abnormal kidney morphology, enlarged heart, absent adrel gland, male infertility
curation_notes: Reverted to Secondary Diseases per user instruction (was ['Tissue-restricted Ciliopathies'])

WDR19.functional_summary: Also known as IFT144. Retrograde IFT-A protein. Ortholog of C.elegans DYF-2 (16957054). Mutations are associated with a broad spectrum of ciliopathies (24504730) including nephronophthisis, Jeune syndrome (22019273), Sensenbrenner syndrome (29134781), asphyxiating thoracic dysplasia (23339108), reti l dystrophies and Caroli desease (23559409). Mutations can also cause disorganization of in sperm flagella and nonsyndromic asthenoteratospermia (32323121)
WDR19.protein_complex: TULP3-Intraflagellar transport complex A; Intraflagellar transport complex A TULP3-IFT122-IFT140-IFT144 subcomplex; Intraflagellar transport complex A core complex; Intraflagellar transport complex A
WDR19.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Senior-Loken syndrome; nephronophthisis; Nephronophthisis; Senior-Loken syndrome 8

WDR35.functional_summary: IFT121. IFT complex A component, endogenous WDR35 localizes to cilia and centrosomes throughout the developing embryo and human and mouse fibroblasts lacking the protein fail to produce cilia. Human and mouse homozygouse mutations in WDR35 cause ciliopathy short-rib polydactyly syndrome (22987818). Heterozygous mutations shown to cause cranioectodermal dysplasia-2. OMIM:613602. Interacts with RagA, mTORC1 activator (30570184)
WDR35.protein_complex: Intraflagellar transport complex A peripheral subcomplex; TULP3-Intraflagellar transport complex A; Intraflagellar transport complex A
WDR35.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Short rib-polydactyly syndrome, Verma-Naumoff type; short rib-polydactyly syndrome, Majewski type
curation_notes: Classical EvC confirmed: PMID 26075268 (Caparros-Martin et al. 2015, specific WDR35 variants cause distinctive EvC by disrupting EvC complex/SMO recruitment)

WDR44.functional_summary: Rab11 binding protein, negatively regulates ciliogenesis. Akt phosphorylates WDR44 at Ser342/344 to stabilise it and increase its binding to Rab11, which prevents ciliogenesis. WDR44 depletion promotes binding of Rab11a to Rabin8, which leads to preciliary trafficking and ciliogenesis- initiating events at the mother centriole. Disruption of Akt sig ling causes a switch from Rab11-WDR44 to the Rab11-FIP3-Rabin8 complex which promotes ciliogenesis(31204173) Endosomal protein phosphorylated by Akt at Ser346 (31665227)
functional_category: Trafficking (BBSome, small GTPases, vesicular transport, ATPases)

WHRN.functional_summary: DFNB31/whirlin. PDZ scaffold protein. Mutated in autosomal recessive non-syndromic deafness type 31 (12833159) and Usher syndrome type 2D (PMID:17171570) in humans (OMIM 607928). Only the whirlin long isoform (with an additio l N-termi l PDZ domain) is expressed in the reti , the reti is affected if this extra PDZ domain is mutated (20502675). Interacts directly with USH2A and VLGR1 in the connecting cilium of photoreceptor cells (16434480). Colocalizes with MPP1 in the reti at the outer limiting membrane, at the outer sy ptic layer and at the basal bodies and the ciliary axoneme of the connecting cilium of the photoreceptors (17584769). Interacts with L-type calcium channel subunit Ca(v)1.3 (alpha(1D) at synpase in reti (19959638). Interacts with RPGR(ORF15) in the photoreceptors (22323458)

ZFYVE19.functional_summary: The Zfyve19-/- mice were normal overall, particularly with respect to hepatobiliary features. However, when challenged with α-naphthyl isothiocyanate, Zfyve19-/- mice developed changes resembling those in ZFYVE19-deficient patients, including elevated serum liver injury markers, increased numbers of bile duct profiles with abnormal cholangiocyte polarity and biliary fibrosis. Failure of cell division, centriole and cilia abnormalities, and increased cell death were observed in knockdown/knockout cells(PMID: 38816193). Zfyve19-/- mice show centriole and cilia abnormalities, cell division failure, and biliary fibrosis via TGF-β pathway. Cholangiocyte polarity disrupted. ZFYVE19 confirmed as liver-restricted ciliopathy gene.

ZIC1.functional_summary: Zic1, perhaps together with Gli1 and Gli3, may act as a link between mechanosensing and Wnt sig ling ( 20354137).

ZIC3.functional_summary: Mutations in the ZIC3 gene cause Visceral Heterotaxy (PMID: 9354794).
ZIC3.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: heterotaxy, visceral, 1, X-linked; VACTERL association, X-linked, with or without hydrocephalus; congenital heart defects, multiple types, 1, X-linked; visceral heterotaxy; congenital heart malformation

ZMYND10.functional_summary: Recessive biallelic mutations in ZMYND10 cause a form of PCD in which patients lack inner dynein arms and outer dynein arms and lack axonemal protein components D H5 and D LI1 from respiratory cilia (CILD22, OMIM:63395) (23891469). Interacts with LRCC6, also a cause of PCD (CILD19, OMIM:614930). LRRC6 mutations abrogate the interaction between the LRRC6 CS domain and the ZMYND10 C-termi l domain (23891469). Colocalizes with SAS6 and PCM at the centriole in rat trachea (23891469). Stabilizes intermediate chain proteins in the cytoplasmic pre-assembly of dynein arms (29601588). Functions in a chaperone relay during axonemal dynein assembly (29916806)

ZNF423.functional_summary: ZNF423 localizes to the ciliary transition zone and is also involved in D damage repair (22863007. The analysis of the tChP in the lateral ventricles revealed that wild-type and mutant cells alike display a columnar and multiciliated epithelium positive for Arl13b+ and γ-tubulin (Fig. S8), again suggesting that Zfp423 (human ZNF423) is only required for the specification of the hChP ciliated epithelium and that alternative regulatory molecules may be in place in the embryonic lateral ventricles. (33046507)
ZNF423.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Joubert syndrome; Joubert syndrome with oculorenal defect

ZRSR2.description: zinc finger CCCH-type, RNA binding motif and serine/arginine rich 2 [Source:HGNC Symbol,Acc:HGNC:23019]
ZRSR2.functional_summary: Mutations in the ZRSR2 gene cause Orofaciodigital Syndrome (PMID: 38158857).

CP.functional_summary: Mutations in CP cause Retinal Degeneration (PMID: 37439255).
CP.protein_complex: CP-LTF-MPO complex; CP-MPO complex; CP-LTF complex

FUZZY.description: fuzzy planar cell polarity protein [Source:HGNC Symbol,Acc:HGNC:26219]
FUZZY.functional_summary: FUZZY (CPLANE4) is a member of the CPLANE (ciliogenesis and planar polarity effector) complex required for ciliogenesis and planar cell polarity. Essential for the assembly of the intraflagellar transport machinery at the ciliary base. Associated with Joubert syndrome and Short-Rib Thoracic Dysplasia.(25336913)

GNRHR.functional_summary: Mutations in GNRHR cause Kallmann Syndrome (PMID: 36138264).
curation_notes: Reverted to Secondary Diseases per user instruction (was ['Tissue-restricted Ciliopathies'])

GUCY2F.functional_summary: Mutations in GUCY2F cause Cone-Rod Dystrophy (PMID: 37361352).

IZUMO1.functional_summary: Mutations in IZUMO1 cause Male infertility (PMID: 27904014).

PRPH.functional_summary: Mutations in PRPH cause Retinal Degeneration (PMID: 11853768).

PSD.description: exchange factor for ARF6, A [Source:HGNC Symbol,Acc:HGNC:19073]
PSD.functional_summary: EFA6A, an exchange factor for the small G protein Arf6, is essential for visual function through its role in photoreceptor cilia. Present in multiple retinal layers including photoreceptors and RPE. Depletion causes morphological and functional defects in photoreceptors resembling retinal ciliopathies, and impairs RPE phagocytic activity. Previously described as a regulator of early ciliogenesis by promoting distal appendage vesicle fusion (PMID:41858616). EFA6A depletion causes morphological and functional defects in photoreceptors resembling retinal ciliopathies; impairs RPE phagocytic activity. Essential for visual function via photoreceptor cilia.
functional_category: Trafficking (BBSome, small GTPases, vesicular transport, ATPases)

SCN1B.functional_summary: Mutations in SCN1B cause Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy (PMID: 39616287).
SCN1B.protein_complex: FGF13-SCN8A-SCN1B complex; SCN9A-SCN1B-SCN2B complex; SCN4A-SCN1B complex
SCN1B.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures-plus; generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures plus

SEZ6.functional_summary: Mutations in SEZ6 cause Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy (PMID: 39616287).

SUMF1.functional_summary: Mutations in SUMF1 cause Retinal Dystrophy (PMID: 38863195).

TNR.functional_summary: Mutations in TNR cause Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy (PMID: 39616287).

DNAH17.functional_summary: Sperm-specific axonemal outer dynein arm heavy chain. Mutations cause isolated male infertility due to asthenozoospermia (31178125) and flagella instability (31658987)
DNAH17.addition_note: Ali I et al. 2024 Mol Genet Genomics 299:69

CFAP43.description: cilia and flagella associated protein 43 [Source:HGNC Symbol,Acc:HGNC:26684]
CFAP43.functional_summary: Formation of flagellar axonemes during spermatogenesis. Contains WD repeat domains, which are highly enriched in the intraflagellar transport proteins of sperm flagella (28552195). Essential for beating, but not rotating left-right organiser (LRO) or immotile cilia. Involved in the regulation of the beating frequency of tracheal cilia (31884020)
CFAP43.addition_note: Coutton C 2018 Nat Commun 9:686; Tang S 2017 AJHG 100:854

CFAP44.description: cilia and flagella associated protein 44 [Source:HGNC Symbol,Acc:HGNC:25631]
CFAP44.functional_summary: Ciliary proteins Fap43 and Fap44 interact with each other and are essential for proper cilia and flagella beating(29687140).
CFAP44.addition_note: Coutton C 2018 Nat Commun 9:686; Tang S 2017 AJHG 100:854

CFAP70.description: cilia and flagella associated protein 70 [Source:HGNC Symbol,Acc:HGNC:30726]
CFAP70.functional_summary: Regulator component of the outer dynein arm in motile cilia and flagella, regulating ciliary motility and length (30158508)

LRRC23.functional_summary: Radial spoke protein with function in ciliary motility and motile cilia formation. Mutations in Lrrc23 result in ciliary motility defects specifically in the cilia of the otic vesicle (29475374).
LRRC23.mouse_ciliopathy_phenotype: increased circulating creatinine level, male infertility
LRRC23.addition_note: Li Y 2023 Clin Genet; Hwang JY 2023 eLife; Zhang X 2021 J Cell Sci

POC1A.functional_summary: Stable component of centrioles that and plays a role in their formation and mainte nce. Mutations cause ciliogenesis defects and impared mitosis, as well as primordial dwarfism (26336158, 23015594, 22840364).
POC1A.addition_note: Shaheen R 2012 AJHG 91:330; Perge K 2024 Eur J Endocrinol 190:151

TTC26.addition_note: Shaheen R 2020 Hepatology; Alfadhel M 2021 Mol Syndromol; Yang W 2025 Pediatr Nephrol

GLIS3.functional_summary: Loss of Glis2 function in mice and mutations in GLIS2 have been associated with nephronophthisis (17618285), while genetic alterations in the GLIS3 gene have been linked to a syndrome characterized by neo tal diabetes and congenital hypothyroidism (NDH) (16715098). Dysfunction of Glis3 leads to the development of cystic re l disease, suggesting that Glis3 plays a critical role in maintaining normal re l functions. Glis3 sig ling pathway have localization to the primary cilium and interaction with Wwtr1(19273592). Glis3 mutant mice form normal primary cilia, but the percentage of cells with a primary cilium in dilated and cystic renal tubules is reduced (19273592) GLIS3 deficiency does not affect the length of the primary cilium in mice, but mutation of Glis3 in Medaka results in shorter cilia (32693112). Glis3 deficiency also resulted in a medaka mutant with shortened renal cilia and caused polycystic kidney disease (Hashimoto et al. 2009).
GLIS3.addition_note: Kang HS 2009 MCB; Dimitri P 2016 AJMG; Rurale G 2025

GPR161.functional_summary: GPR161 increases cAMP levels, establishing the basal cAMP gradient and activation of PKA. Repression of Shh sig ling by determining the processing of Gli3 to its repressor form (23332756).

XPNPEP3.functional_summary: Mitochondrial protein expressed specifically in distal convoluted tubule and cortical collecting duct cells. Homozygous frameshift and splice-site mutations cause an autosomal recessive nephronophisis-like nephropathy in humans (OMIM:613553), 20179356. targeted to mitochondria by an amino- termi l mitochondrial sig l sequence. Has N-termi l proline cleavage activity. E.coli ortholog can can efficiently cleave CEP290/NPHP6, ALMS1, and LRRC50 N-terminus. Cleavage of N-terminus of LRRC50 is essential for normal gastrulation in zebrafish ( 20179356)

CEP250.functional_summary: Interact with proteins implicated in rhodopsin trafficking (NEK2 and NINL). Rrecruitment of several proteins to centriole proximal ends, including Girdin (Girders of actin filaments) and proteins that associate with the distal region of the mother centriole (NEK2, ninein, CEP170, p150glued and KIF2A) (30421101). C- P1 anchores rootletin filaments that hold duplicated centrosomes together(28100636). Mutations are associated to Usher Syndrome and retinitis pigmentosa (28005958).
functional_category: Trafficking (BBSome, small GTPases, vesicular transport, ATPases)
CEP250.mouse_ciliopathy_phenotype: male infertility, abnormal auditory brainstem response

SEC61B.functional_summary: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in SEC61B were identified in autosomal dominant polycystic liver disease (ADPLD) by Besse et al. 2017 (PMID: 28375157). SEC61B is part of the protein biogenesis pathway in the endoplasmic reticulum; loss of SEC61B function impairs maturation and trafficking of polycystin-1, leading to hepatic cyst formation. The gene was identified after exome sequencing in a cohort of PCLD patients without PRKCSH or SEC63 mutations, alongside ALG8 and GANAB.
SEC61B.addition_source: Besse et al. 2017 J Clin Invest PMID:28375157

PRMT9.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Bi-allelic loss-of-function variants cause syndromic intellectual disability with global developmental delay, autism, epilepsy, hypotonia. Patient fibroblasts show abnormal primary cilia length under ciliogenesis conditions.
PRMT9.functional_summary: Protein arginine methyltransferase suspected to function in alternative splicing through SF3B2 interaction. PRMT9 has a role in ciliogenesis demonstrated by altered cilia length in patient fibroblasts (Kröll-Hermi et al. 2025, PMID 41260215).

WDR47.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Bi-allelic variants cause complex neurodevelopmental syndrome with corpus callosum agenesis, microcephaly, enlarged ventricles. Heterozygous variants associated with cardiovascular laterality defects.
WDR47.functional_summary: WDR47 cooperates with Camsaps and Katanin to generate ciliary central microtubules. Wdr47 deficiency in mouse multiciliated ependymal cells results in complete loss of central pair, rotatory beat, and primary ciliary dyskinesia (Liu et al. 2021, PMID 34608154). C. elegans homolog NMTN-1 is required for ciliogenesis of AWB chemosensory neurons (Song et al. 2022, PMID 36453135). Bi-allelic human variants cause neurodevelopmental syndrome (Bayam et al. 2025, PMID 39609633).

CIROZ.description: Cilia and flagella associated protein, formerly C1orf127; ZP-N domain-containing protein required for left-right organizer function
CIROZ.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Bi-allelic CIROZ inactivation variants cause heterotaxy with congenital heart defects in 16 individuals from 10 families.
CIROZ.functional_summary: CIROZ (formerly C1orf127) encodes a protein with signal peptide and 3 zona pellucida N domains expressed specifically in the left-right organizer of mice, frogs, and fish. Forms a genetic module with DAND5, PKD1L1, MMP21, and CIROP in motile cilia of the LRO (Szenker-Ravi et al. 2025, PMID 39753129).

RAB35.description: Member RAS oncogene family — small GTPase regulating endosomal trafficking and ciliogenesis
RAB35.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Homozygous missense variant (R27H) causes global developmental delay, hydrocephalus, Dandy-Walker malformation, axial hypotonia with peripheral hypertonia, visual problems, conductive hearing impairment.
RAB35.functional_summary: Small GTPase regulating endosomal membrane trafficking, primary cilia formation, and cytokinesis. Loss-of-function R27H variant impairs Rab35 effector binding (MICAL1), drives Arf6 activation, and causes altered length, number, and ARL13B composition of primary cilia (Aguila et al. 2024, PMID 38432637).

TEDC1.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Bi-allelic loss-of-function variants cause prenatal-onset severe growth impairment, primary microcephaly, developmental delay, adrenal insufficiency, congenital glaucoma, delayed bone aging, craniosynostosis, congenital tracheal stenosis, primary hypogonadism.
TEDC1.functional_summary: TEDC1 partners with TEDC2 for centriole stability and cell proliferation. Bi-allelic TEDC1 deletion causes cilia abnormalities through defective acetylated tubulins. tedc1-/- zebrafish recapitulates growth impairment and cranial bone dysplasia (Miyake et al. 2025, PMID 39979680).

KICS2.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Bi-allelic variants in KICS2 cause intellectual disability and epilepsy (11 affected individuals).
KICS2.functional_summary: Component of KICSTOR complex regulating mTORC1 in response to nutrient deprivation. Variants compromise KICSTOR complex formation and impact mTORC1 proteome including ciliogenesis-related proteins. Kics2 depletion in zebrafish causes ciliary dysfunction (Buchert et al. 2025, PMID 39824192).

MBD5.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Severe epilepsy and intellectual disability associated with MBD5 disruption.
MBD5.functional_summary: MBD5 haploinsufficiency disrupts primary cilium-related processes during early cortical development. Patient-derived neural progenitor cells show decreased length and number of primary cilia (Martins et al. 2023, PMID 37628781).

TAOK1.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: ASD and CHD risk gene; impairs primary cilia formation.
TAOK1.functional_summary: Identified in CRISPRi screen of CHD genes disrupting NPC biology; one of seven ASD+CHD genes (CEP290, CHD4, KMT2E, NSD1, OFD1, RFX3, TAOK1) impairing primary cilia formation in vitro. In vivo Xenopus tropicalis investigation confirms role in motile cilia formation and heart development (Teerikorpi et al. 2025, PMID 40552535).

TAOK2.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Autism spectrum disorder associated with 16p11.2 copy number variation.
TAOK2.functional_summary: TAOK2 protein kinase regulates primary cilium length. NPCs from 16p11.2 deletion carriers show longer primary cilia; duplication carriers show stunted cilia. TAOK2-deficient NPCs exhibit elongated cilia, aberrant IFT88 and pericentrin accumulation, and impaired Sonic Hedgehog signaling (Byeon et al. 2025, PMID 40882641).

MYH10.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Heterozygous MYH10 variants cause broad spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders and variable congenital anomalies affecting most organ systems (16 individuals).
MYH10.functional_summary: Non-muscle myosin II heavy chain. MYH10 knockout cells show defects in primary ciliogenesis and reduced ciliary length with impaired Hedgehog signaling. MYH10 variant overexpression produces dominant-negative effect on ciliary length (Holtz et al. 2022, PMID 35980381).

GNAI1.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Mutations cause developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, epilepsy.
GNAI1.functional_summary: Heterotrimeric G protein alpha subunit. GNAI1 is required for ciliogenesis in human cells. Disorder variants (T48I, K272R, A328P, V334E) impact cilia assembly and function in C. elegans AWC neurons; D173V/D175V disrupts ciliary localization in human ciliated cell lines (Salama et al. 2025, PMID 41052774).

FSD1L.description: Fibronectin type III and SPRY domain-containing 1-like
FSD1L.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Bi-allelic pathogenic variants cause severe hydrocephalus, corpus callosum agenesis, and absent pyramid decussation OR neurodevelopmental syndrome with severe intellectual disability, spastic tetraparesis, reduced vision, epilepsy, and corpus callosum agenesis/hypoplasia (11 individuals from 6 families).
FSD1L.functional_summary: FSD1L localizes to the mitotic spindle during M phase and to the transition zone and along the axoneme of the primary cilium during interphase. Patient fibroblasts show marked mitotic spindle alterations and reduced ciliogenesis and ciliary length. Phenotype overlaps with L1 syndrome (Serpieri et al. 2026, AJHG DOI 10.1016/j.ajhg.2026.01.014).

CDKL5.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: CDKL5 Deficiency Disorder (CDD): epileptic encephalopathy affecting young children.
CDKL5.functional_summary: Protein kinase. CDKL5 phosphorylates PPP1R35, which is critical for centriole elongation and cilia morphology — processes that are impaired in CDD. CDKL5 also phospho-targets CEP131 (Massey et al. 2024, PMID 39136782).

GPR75.functional_summary: GPR75 is a brain-expressed orphan G protein-coupled receptor that localizes to the primary cilia of hypothalamic cells and regulates food intake and body weight. Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in GPR75 are associated with lower body mass index (BMI) in large-scale human exome-sequencing studies. Gpr75-knockout mice display reduced body weight, reduced fat weight, and reduced food intake under high-fat diet. GPR75 interacts with Gαq to activate signaling pathways. The Thinner missense allele (L144P) and human BMI-lowering variants fail to localize to the cilium, demonstrating that ciliary localization is required for GPR75 function in body-weight homeostasis. Loss of GPR75 fails to suppress obesity in Lepob or Adcy3-mutant mice, suggesting GPR75 acts upstream of leptin and adenylate cyclase 3 pathways. Reference: Jiang et al. 2024, J Clin Invest, PMID 39137039.
GPR75.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: GPR75 loss-of-function variants associated with reduced BMI in humans (lean phenotype, opposite of MC4R loss-of-function obesity).
GPR75.mouse_ciliopathy_phenotype: Gpr75-/- mice: reduced body weight, reduced fat, reduced food intake on HFD. Thinner allele (L144P) loses ciliary localization.
GPR75.addition_source: Jiang et al. 2024 J Clin Invest PMID 39137039
curation_notes: GPR75 is a ciliary GPCR controlling body weight via the hypothalamus, comparable to MC4R/ADCY3/TUB but with loss-of-function leading to leanness rather than obesity.

Phenotype direction: protective (low BMI). Grouped with Ciliary Monogenic Obesity because GPR75 is a ciliary GPCR in the same hypothalamic neuronal signalling axis as MC4R, but its loss reduces BMI rather than causing obesity (Jiang et al. 2024, PMID 39137039).
GPR75.protective_allele_note: Loss-of-function variants in GPR75 PROTECT against obesity (lower BMI), opposite to the obesity-causing direction of MC4R, ADCY3, TUB, and CEP19. GPR75 is grouped under "Ciliary Monogenic Obesity" because it is a ciliary GPCR in the same hypothalamic energy-balance signalling axis as MC4R, but readers should note the protective (BMI-lowering) phenotypic direction rather than disease-causing.

HSD17B4.functional_summary: Peroxisomal bifunctional enzyme involved in fatty acid β-oxidation and steroid metabolism. HSD17B4 deficiency causes dysregulation of primary cilia: patient fibroblasts show reduced cilia number and shortened cilia, and Hsd17b4-knockout mice show motor dysfunction and Purkinje cell loss with impaired primary cilia formation. Acetate administration rescues cilia formation and motor function in mouse models, suggesting acetyl-CoA-mediated regulation of ciliogenesis (Bae et al. 2025).
HSD17B4.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: D-bifunctional protein deficiency: neonatal-onset peroxisomal disorder with severe neurological symptoms, leukodystrophy, accumulation of very long-chain fatty acids; Perrault syndrome 1: sensorineural hearing loss, ovarian dysgenesis (in females), cerebellar ataxia.
HSD17B4.mouse_ciliopathy_phenotype: Hsd17b4-knockout mice: motor dysfunction, Purkinje cell loss, impaired primary cilia formation; rescued by acetate administration.
HSD17B4.addition_note: Bae et al. 2025 Nat Commun (PMID 40102401) demonstrated ciliopathy mechanism in HSD17B4-deficient patient fibroblasts and mouse model. Established human diseases: D-bifunctional protein deficiency (DBPD; OMIM 261515) and Perrault syndrome 1 (PRLTS1; OMIM 233400).

ciliopathies: Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Microcephaly, Arthrogryposis, and Structural Brain Anomalies
SMPD4.functional_summary: Neutral sphingomyelinase that metabolises sphingomyelin into ceramide at the nuclear envelope and ER. Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) show shortened and bulbous primary cilia, rescued by exogenous ceramide treatment. Smpd4-null and forebrain-specific knockout mice exhibit cerebellar hypoplasia from Purkinje cell loss. Patient iPSC-derived neural rosettes and organoids show reduced neural progenitor cells, decreased proliferation, and increased cell death (Inskeep et al. 2024).
SMPD4.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: Severe neurodevelopmental disorder: microcephaly (primary or progressive), cerebellar hypoplasia, hypomyelination, simplified gyral pattern, hypoplasia of corpus callosum and brain stem, intrauterine growth restriction, congenital arthrogryposis, neonatal respiratory distress; some surviving individuals develop insulin-dependent diabetes. 23 individuals from 12 families reported.
SMPD4.mouse_ciliopathy_phenotype: Smpd4-null mice: cerebellar hypoplasia, perinatal lethality (incomplete penetrance), failure to thrive, Purkinje cell loss. Conditional KO Purkinje cell cilia longer than wild-type.
SMPD4.addition_note: Inskeep et al. 2024 Development (PMID 39470011) demonstrated ciliary mechanism in patient-derived iPSCs and mouse model with ceramide rescue. Established human disease: NEDMABA (Magini et al. 2019, PMID 30962623), 23 individuals from 12 families.

PRPF6.functional_summary: Encodes essential component of the U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP for pre-mRNA splicing. Mutations cause autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa via impaired tri-snRNP assembly and stability (PMID 21549338). Together with PRPF3, PRPF8, PRPF31, and SNRNP200, the PRPF/snRNP200 module establishes the splicing-factor retinitis pigmentosa class within the broader spliceosome-ciliopathy interface.

CWC27.functional_summary: Encodes spliceosome-associated cyclophilin (peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase) of the Bact spliceosome complex. Mutations cause retinitis pigmentosa with or without skeletal anomalies (RPSKA, OMIM 250410), spanning isolated retinal degeneration to syndromic forms with brachydactyly, craniofacial abnormalities, short stature, and developmental delay (PMID 28285769). Identified as a hit in genome-scale ciliogenesis screens (Breslow 2018), supporting the classification of CWC27-associated disease as a ciliopathy.
CWC27.human_ciliopathy_phenotype: retinitis pigmentosa with or without skeletal anomalies (RPSKA)
CWC27.mouse_ciliopathy_phenotype: Cwc27 K338fs mice show progressive retinal degeneration with splicing defects (PMID 34726245)

SON.description: SON DNA and RNA binding protein [Source:HGNC Symbol;Acc:HGNC:11183]
SON.functional_summary: Encodes a nuclear RNA splicing factor that promotes pre-mRNA splicing of many genes essential for development. Heterozygous loss-of-function variants cause Zhu-Tokita-Takenouchi-Kim (ZTTK) syndrome (OMIM 617140), a multisystem developmental disorder characterised by intellectual disability, craniofacial dysmorphism, brain malformation, musculoskeletal abnormalities, and congenital heart and genitourinary defects. SON is required for procentriole assembly and ciliogenesis through proper splicing and expression of CEP131, a major centriolar satellite protein (PMID 34406792).
SON.mouse_ciliopathy_phenotype: Son+/- mice recapitulate ZTTK phenotype: growth retardation, cognitive impairment, skeletal abnormalities, kidney agenesis (PMID 38516884)

TTLL11.functional_summary: Tubulin polyglutamylase that elongates the polyglutamate side chain on alpha-tubulin, a post-translational modification critical for ciliary axoneme integrity, intraflagellar transport, and Hedgehog signaling. Loss-of-function variant c.1569_1570insTT identified as the causative variant for AIS in a five-generation UK family; primary cilia from affected individuals were shorter, less abundant, and less polyglutamylated than controls. Zebrafish ttll11 morphants and CRISPR mutants show 3D spinal curvature and retinal cone layer disorganization (34040021).
TTLL11.mouse_ciliopathy_phenotype: abnormal heart morphology; enlarged heart; abnormal spleen morphology; abnormal skin morphology

synonyms: Kartagener Syndrome (subset with situs inversus + bronchiectasis + sinusitis)
Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.notes: Kartagener syndrome is a phenotypic subset, not a separate disease. 'Immotile cilia syndrome' is outdated since many PCD cases involve dyskinetic (not absent) motility.

synonyms: Multiple Morphological Abnormalities of the sperm Flagella (MMAF)
Male Infertility.notes: Encompasses MMAF, dysplasia of fibrous sheath, and sperm flagellum-specific axonemal defects. Separate from broader male infertility (which has many non-cilia causes).

synonyms: Reduced Generation of Multiple Motile Cilia (RGMC)
Mucociliary Clearance Disorder.omim_preferred: Ciliary Dyskinesia, Primary, with or without Defective Multiple Motile Ciliogenesis (CILD-MMC)
Mucociliary Clearance Disorder.notes: Caused by defects in MCIDAS, CCNO, FOXJ1; characterized by failure to generate multiple motile cilia (vs. PCD where cilia are present but dysfunctional).

Joubert Syndrome.notes: JSRD encompasses Joubert syndrome plus its multi-system variants (Joubert with retinal, renal, hepatic involvement); some authors split these but most modern catalogues unify under JSRD.

Bardet-Biedl Syndrome.notes: Historically grouped with Laurence-Moon syndrome; modern OMIM keeps them distinct. McKusick-Kaufman syndrome (MKKS) is an allelic variant.

synonyms: Medullary Cystic Kidney Disease (related but distinct in adult-onset forms)
Nephronophthisis.notes: Includes infantile, juvenile, and adolescent forms. Senior-Løken syndrome is NPHP + retinal degeneration.

synonyms: Jeune Asphyxiating Thoracic Dystrophy (a SRTD subtype)
Short-Rib Thoracic Dysplasia.notes: Modern classification subsumes the older Saldino-Noonan/Majewski/Verma-Naumoff/Beemer-Langer SRPS types under SRTD.

Orofaciodigital Syndrome.notes: OFD type 1 is X-linked (OFD1 gene); OFD types II–XIV are autosomal recessive.

Ellis-van Creveld Syndrome.merge_note: 2026-06-29: merged 'Ellis-van Creveld Syndrome-like phenotype' (DYNC2H1, PRKACA, PRKACB) and 'Ellis-van Creveld Syndrome-like phenotypes' (GLI3) into the canonical entry. The two variant names are kept as synonyms.

Weyers Acrofacial Dysostosis.notes: Allelic with Ellis-van Creveld syndrome (same EVC/EVC2 genes); milder dominant form.

synonyms: Cerebellar vermis hypoplasia, Oligophrenia, Ataxia, Coloboma, Hepatic fibrosis (acronym)
Joubert Syndrome with Hepatic Defect (JSRD subtype)
COACH Syndrome.omim_preferred: Joubert Syndrome with Congenital Hepatic Fibrosis (JBTS-CHF) / COACH Syndrome
COACH Syndrome.notes: Modern view: COACH is a JSRD subtype (Joubert syndrome + hepatic involvement).

synonyms: Cerebro-Acro-Visceral Early lethality syndrome (historical, distinct usage)

McKusick-Kaufman Syndrome.notes: Allelic with Bardet-Biedl syndrome 6 (BBS6) — same MKKS gene.

Laurence-Moon Syndrome.notes: Historically grouped with BBS. Modern OMIM defines it as PNPLA6-related: spastic paraplegia + retinal degeneration + hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, distinct from BBS (no obesity, no polydactyly).

synonyms: Apple Peel Syndrome (related: features intestinal atresia)
Retinitis pigmentosa, Hypopituitarism, Nephronophthisis, Skeletal dysplasia (acronym)

Seckel-like Syndrome.notes: Related to Seckel syndrome but with cilia-specific etiology.

synonyms: Bone fragility, with Renal failure, ENcephalopathy, and Skeletal dysplasia
Short stature, Onychodysplasia, Facial dysmorphism, hypoTrichosis (acronym)

Retinal Dystrophy/Degeneration.notes: Umbrella entry covering RP, syndromic and non-syndromic IRDs with ciliary etiology.

Retinal Ciliopathy.notes: 1-gene entry (CEP162). Could be subsumed under Retinal Dystrophy/Degeneration.

Non-syndromic Retinal Degeneration.notes: 1-gene entry (SCLT1). Could be subsumed under Retinal Dystrophy/Degeneration.

Skeletal Ciliopathy.notes: Umbrella entry. Overlaps heavily with Short-Rib Thoracic Dysplasia and Ellis-van Creveld.

Medulloblastoma.notes: SHH-subgroup medulloblastomas have ciliary etiology; other subgroups (WNT, Group 3, Group 4) do not.

Kallmann Syndrome.omim_preferred: Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism with or without Anosmia (Kallmann syndrome)

Ciliary Monogenic Obesity.notes: Includes MC4R, ADCY3, TUB, CEP19 (loss-of-function → obesity); GPR75 has opposite (protective) phenotypic direction.

synonyms: Non-motile Hydrocephalus (in this catalogue, distinguishes from PCD-associated)

Synpolydactyly, Polycystic Kidney Diseas.notes: IFT70A-related; same gene also in Synpolydactyly. Likely a phenotypic-extension variant of Synpolydactyly.

synonyms: Infantile Polycystic Kidney Disease (historical, often used synonymously)
Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Di.omim_preferred: Polycystic Kidney and Hepatic Disease, Autosomal Recessive

Polycystic Kidney Disease.notes: Generic / catch-all entry; overlaps with ADPKD/ARPKD. Genes here are mostly syndromic-CKD or atypical PKD presentations.

synonyms: Often synonymous with ARPKD in earlier literature
Infantile Polycystic Kidney Disease.notes: Overlaps with ARPKD; some authors consider these synonymous. Verify dataset placement of HNF1B, TSC1, TSC2 (these are syndromic forms, not classic ARPKD).

Bilateral Polycystic Kidney Disease.notes: 1-gene entry (TTC21B). Likely candidate for merging with PKD or syndromic kidney entry.

Cystic Kidney Disease.notes: Broad entry overlapping with all PKD entries.

Cystic Renal Dysplasia.notes: 1-gene entry (BICC1). BICC1 also in Cystic Kidney Disease — likely duplicate.

synonyms: Communicating Cavernous Ectasia of Intrahepatic Bile Ducts
Caroli Syndrome (when associated with congenital hepatic fibrosis)

Renal Cell Carcinoma.notes: Cilia link via HIF/VHL; subset of RCC has ciliary etiology.

Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.notes: Cilia link narrow; most COPD is environmental, not genetic.

Primary Endocardial Fibroelastosis.notes: 1-gene entry (ALMS1) — shares gene with Alström syndrome.

Nonsyndromic Tetralogy of Fallot.notes: Defined by cardiac OFT defects (overriding aorta + VSD + pulmonary stenosis + RVH) without extracardiac features. Distinct from syndromic CHD genes that present as part of broader multisystem ciliopathies.

D-Bifunctional Protein Deficiency.notes: Autosomal-recessive peroxisomal β-oxidation disorder caused by HSD17B4 mutations; generally fatal within the first two years of life. Ciliopathy mechanism established by Bae et al. 2025 (Nat Commun).

Perrault Syndrome.notes: Autosomal-recessive disorder; sensorineural hearing loss in both sexes plus ovarian dysgenesis in females, sometimes with neurological manifestations including ataxia. Caused by HSD17B4 (and other genes). Ciliopathy mechanism established by Bae et al. 2025 (Nat Commun).

synonyms: Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Structural Brain Anomalies and Insulin-Dependent Diabetes (subset)
Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Microce.omim_preferred: Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Microcephaly, Arthrogryposis, and Structural Brain Anomalies
Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Microce.notes: Autosomal-recessive disorder caused by SMPD4 mutations; severe developmental brain malformations including microcephaly and cerebellar hypoplasia, congenital arthrogryposis, intrauterine growth restriction, severe developmental delay; some surviving individuals develop insulin-dependent diabetes. Ciliopathy mechanism established by Inskeep et al. 2024 (Development).

synonyms: Mental Retardation, Truncal Obesity, Retinal Dystrophy, and Micropenis Syndrome
MORM Syndrome.notes: Autosomal-recessive ciliopathy caused by INPP5E mutations; truncal obesity, retinal dystrophy, micropenis, intellectual disability. Phenotypically overlaps with Joubert syndrome (also INPP5E-related).

synonyms: Multinucleated Neurons, Anhydramnios, Renal Dysplasia, Cerebellar Hypoplasia, and Hydranencephaly
MARCH Syndrome.notes: Autosomal-recessive lethal ciliopathy caused by CEP55 mutations; multi-organ developmental defects including renal dysplasia, hydranencephaly, cerebellar hypoplasia, anhydramnios.

Morbid Obesity and Spermatogenic Failure.notes: Autosomal-recessive obesity-infertility syndrome caused by CEP19 mutations.

Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis.notes: OMIM #181800. Spine deformity (Cobb angle >=10 degrees) emerging in adolescence (~3% prevalence). Associated with susceptibility variants in ciliary genes POC5 and TTLL11; supported by mouse and zebrafish models of primary cilium dysfunction.
